grades.quote: All floating-point operations that perform rounding can select the rounding mode using the _rm_ field with the encoding shown in Table 25.
grades.reason: States that rounding operations select their rounding mode via the instruction's rm field, but it doesn't mention frm or the dynamic (DYN) encoding. It also refers to an encoding table that isn't included, so it covers only part of the relationship.

grades.quote: |FMADD.S|rs1, rs2, rs3, frm*|rd|NV, OF, UF, NX|*if rm=111|
grades.reason: A register-dependency table. It indirectly shows that frm is a source register only when rm=111, which hints at the rm/frm relationship. It never explains rounding-mode selection.
The CSR address map only identifies frm as the floating-point dynamic rounding mode register. It says nothing about how rm and frm interact to select the mode.

grades.quote: As with other scalar floating-point instructions, the rounding mode field `rm` can also take on the `DYN` encoding, which indicates that the instruction uses the rounding mode specified in the `frm` CSR.
grades.reason: Directly explains that the rm field in scalar instructions selects a static rounding mode (encodings 000–100). The DYN encoding (111) makes the instruction use the mode held in the frm CSR. It is written for BF16 but says it applies as with other scalar FP instructions.
